questions.question: Describe what the Sun is and what it gives out.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is a star. It is a giant ball of very hot, glowing gas, not solid rock. It makes energy deep inside its centre and gives out heat and light.

questions.question: The Sun is much bigger than the Earth, so why does it look so small in the sky?
questions.expected_answer: The Sun looks small because it is very far away, about one hundred and fifty million kilometres from the Earth. Things that are far away always look smaller than they really are. In fact, the Sun is more than one hundred times wider than the Earth.

questions.question: Explain why the Sun looks so much bigger and brighter than the other stars.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is the closest star to the Earth. All the other stars are much, much further away, so they look like tiny points of light. Some of them are even bigger than the Sun, but they are so far away that they look small.
